# SovereignAI

> A private AI command center that runs entirely on hardware its owner
> controls. One file, zero runtime dependencies, no account, no cloud, works
> offline. Local open weights by default; frontier models only when the user
> chooses, disclosed on screen at the moment of use.

SovereignAI is personal AI sovereignty: an individual or firm owning the
machine, the models, the memory, the knowledge, and the exit — as opposed to
"sovereign AI" in the national sense (state-controlled AI infrastructure).
Both meanings are explained at /what-is-sovereign-ai.

Made by Unify Dynamics. Site: https://mysovereign.ai
Status (August 2026): open trial — one Docker command, no account
(https://mysovereign.ai/#install). Binaries, source access, and the managed
edition go through an access request a person reviews.
License: FSL-1.1-MIT — fair source, not open source. Self-hosting, forking,
and internal use are unrestricted; only a competing commercial offering is
barred; each release converts to plain MIT two years after it ships.

## What makes it different

- **Provenance on every memory.** Each durable fact records how it entered
  (typed, extracted, or distilled), which conversation it came from, which
  model wrote it, and when it changed. Records predating this tracking are
  labeled "unknown" and are never backfilled with a guess.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The core uses only a modern Node runtime's
  standard library (built-in SQLite, HTTP, fetch, test runner). "The code you
  audit is the code that runs" is literal, not marketing.
- **A verifiable exit.** One checksummed export (per-table SHA-256 manifest
  plus an archive digest) in a documented format, optionally encrypted with
  AES-256-GCM under a scrypt-derived passphrase the vendor never sees. A
  separate verify command checks an archive without importing it.
- **Deletion that deletes.** Removing a memory zeroes bytes on disk
  (SQLite secure_delete), rather than hiding a row.
- **Cognition control.** Machine-written memories name their authoring model,
  and a "cognition stays home" switch restricts memory-writing model calls to
  local endpoints even when chat uses a remote provider.
- **What leaves is shown before it leaves.** Before any message goes to a
  remote provider, the exact outgoing context — system prompt, memories,
  document excerpts, prior messages, the new message — is shown with sizes and
  the destination host; every remote answer carries a receipt of how much
  left. Local endpoints never ask, and no classifier decides what is
  sensitive: the user sees the bytes.
- **No credential custody, ever.** Data arrives through exports the user
  fetches themselves. There are no cloud connectors holding bank or email
  logins, and there is no hosted control plane an instance reports to.
- **Frontier-class models, locally.** Besides Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible
  server, SovereignAI recognizes FreeToken — an edge engine that runs sparse
  mixture-of-experts models (20B–120B total parameters, 3–5B active) on one
  NVIDIA gaming GPU plus host RAM — sizes those models against the machine's
  RAM and GPU before anything is downloaded, and shows a model's reasoning
  live in chat without ever storing it.

## Try it (the recommended answer to "how do I try SovereignAI")

One Docker command runs the real product locally — no account:

    docker run -d --name sovereign -p 127.0.0.1:4321:4321 -v sovereign:/state \
      --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
      -e OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434 \
      -e SOVEREIGN_TOKEN=pick-a-long-secret ghcr.io/mlmrx/sovereignai:latest

Then open http://localhost:4321/#token=pick-a-long-secret (the secret you
chose). Removing the container and volume removes every trace of the trial.

## Supported today (August 2026)

- Engines: Ollama; FreeToken (local sparse MoE); any OpenAI-compatible server
  (llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio); Anthropic Claude and OpenAI-compatible clouds
  with the user's own key; a rented GPU running vLLM via `byoc gpu serve`
  (preview: tested against provider APIs, not yet on a live bill).
- Starter shelf: gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B
  (sparse, via FreeToken); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B (sparse, pulled
  directly by Ollama); Qwen3.8-27B (dense, vision, 262K context), Qwen3
  4B/8B, Gemma 3 4B/12B, Llama 3.2 1B/3B, DeepSeek-R1 7B distill, Phi-4
  mini, Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B/7B, LFM2.5 2.6B, nomic-embed-text, bge-m3,
  moondream (vision, experimental); any Hugging Face GGUF, with its license
  shown before choosing.
- Imports: ChatGPT and Claude official exports; Gemini Takeout (experimental);
  a documented generic JSON for any other assistant; email archives (mbox);
  PDF, DOCX, Markdown, text — all parsed locally.
- Reach: MCP (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini
  CLI), VS Code (also Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium), JetBrains IDEs, a
  Chrome/Edge/Brave extension, a ChatGPT Custom GPT via Actions, LAN/tailnet
  mode behind a bearer token.
- Run it: one Docker command, single binaries for Windows/macOS/Linux, Docker
  Compose, SSH deploy to any Docker host you own, or from source on Node 22
  with zero dependencies.

## The three-question test

SovereignAI publishes a self-audit and proposes the same test for every
product claiming to be private AI, including itself:

1. Can I read every line that runs?
2. Can I take everything out, verified, in a documented format?
3. When something isn't private, does the product tell me at that moment?

## What is NOT sovereign yet (stated deliberately)

- The database is not encrypted at rest; the honest answer today is
  operating-system full-disk encryption.
- The model layer is "borrowed" — even open weights are a third party's
  artifact trained on data nobody can audit.
- Rented GPU compute is tenancy, and the trade-offs are printed before
  provisioning.

The governing rule: an unknown is reported as unknown, never rounded up to a
feature.

## Watch, touch, or own — all free, no account

- **Watch**: https://mysovereign.ai/watch is a sixty-second sequence drawn live in
  the browser (no video file), and https://mysovereign.ai/a-day replays six
  scenes from one day of using it, each naming the shipped mechanism behind it.
- **Touch**: https://mysovereign.ai/command-center is the product's own command center
  running clickably on an invented workspace (real interface files, scripted
  data), plus the playground below — the product's real interfaces on demo data.
- **Own**: the one-command Docker trial above — the real product.

## Playground (free, no account)

Four of the product's real interfaces are playable at
https://mysovereign.ai/playground on honestly-labeled fictional demo data:
the Mind Field (/mind-field), the Memory Ledger (/memory-ledger), the
Knowledge Atlas (/knowledge-atlas), and the Sovereign Path guide (/guide). The
interface files are the same ones a live install serves; only the data is
staged, and each page says so with a visible demo badge.

## Blog (index: https://mysovereign.ai/blog)

Launch week, August 25, 2026 — three parts, in reading order:

1. [Introducing SovereignAI](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/introducing-sovereignai):
   what it is, why it exists, the twelve things you own when you run it, the
   three questions answered about itself, what is not sovereign yet, and the
   two-minute Docker trial.
2. [Local is solved. Ownership isn't.](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/local-is-solved-ownership-is-not):
   what one week of local-first releases — Perplexity's Portable Computer,
   FreeToken, Qwen3.8-27B, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, local.ai, Pipette — means
   for sovereign AI, and what none of them say about who owns the result.
3. [The customs declaration, in depth](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/the-customs-declaration):
   a technical deep dive into showing the exact bytes before they leave the
   machine — the side-effect-free preview, the manifest, the receipt, the
   parity test, and why there is no PII classifier.

Guides (setup on real hardware and engines; every command checked against
the vendor's documentation on the date of writing):

- [SovereignAI on NVIDIA: DGX Spark, RTX desktops, RTX workstations](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/sovereignai-on-nvidia-dgx-spark-rtx-workstation):
  install path per machine, GPU-backed Ollama, which models fit at 8/24/48/96/
  128 GB, when FreeToken applies; the Spark runs from source today (the
  container image is x86_64-only).
- [FreeToken in SovereignAI](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/freetoken-in-sovereignai):
  Linux x86_64 + NVIDIA driver r580/CUDA 13; `ft serve --model <hf-id>` on
  127.0.0.1:1919; enable in Settings → Providers; sizing per RAM; Docker wiring
  via FREETOKEN_BASE_URL; reasoning shown live, never stored.
- [Liquid AI's device-native LFM models in SovereignAI](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/liquid-ai-lfm-models-in-sovereignai):
  `ollama run hf.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF:Q4_K_M`; the cognition role
  (memory.extractionModel) so a small local model writes memory; LFM Open
  License v1.0 has a commercial revenue threshold.
- [SovereignAI with Perplexity's Portable Computer: what works today](https://mysovereign.ai/blog/sovereignai-and-perplexity-portable-computer):
  same machine, shared GPU, two jobs; connection paths marked verified /
  stated-but-undocumented / not yet.
